meta.purpose: Ontology layer for cross-country taxonomy answers: framework profiles, a same-activity crosswalk, and a metric-by-metric comparison table.
how_to_use: profiles: load all of it for any cross-country question.

metrics.clusters: the same activity across frameworks with each framework's numeric thresholds, plus frameworks_with_no_numeric_threshold — say that explicitly rather than leaving a country out of the comparison.
crosswalk.links with status curated or confident are safe to state as 'the same activity'. status review means a human has not checked it — do not present those as equivalences.
frameworks.<id>.activities: full records for UMOA, Kyrgyzstan and the Philippines. EU and Korea activities come from their own files.
warnings: Compare structure BEFORE comparing strictness. A threshold framework and an activity-list framework cannot be ranked by strictness — one has no numbers.

Decimal separators differ. The EU and francophone documents use a comma as the decimal point (1,331 = 1.331); English-language documents use it as a thousands separator. Read the framework's decimal_separator before quoting any number.
Never cite an activity by its bare number. '4.5' means different activities in different EU annexes and in different frameworks. Always cite the full uid.

objectives_local: Sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources
Protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems
notes: One record per objective-activity pair: the Regulation states separate criteria per objective.

profiles.name: K-Taxonomy
profiles.issuer: Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (기후에너지환경부)
profiles.structure_note_ko: 활동마다 수치 임계값이 규정에 박혀 있다. 다른 임계값형과 숫자를 직접 견줄 수 있다.
notes: Korea places minimum safeguards inside the activity-level criteria; the EU keeps them outside the delegated acts (Regulation (EU) 2020/852 Art. 18), so EU activity records have no such field.
Korea's Transitional Area (전환부문, 7 activities) is recorded as activity_role=transitional.
Most exclusion criteria cross-refer to the guideline's attachments (붙임) rather than stating numbers inline, so few thresholds are extractable from them.

profiles.name: Green Taxonomy of the Kyrgyz Republic (pilot national classifier)
profiles.issuer: Kyrgyz Republic (Приложение — пилотный общенациональный классификатор)
profiles.legal_basis: Пилотный общенациональный классификатор – Зеленая таксономия Кыргызской Республики (2025), Приложение
profiles.structure_note_ko: 기술·장비·물품 단위까지 내려가고 관세 코드가 붙는다. 세제 혜택 집행 도구라서 '무엇이 녹색인가'보다 '무엇을 면세로 들여올 수 있는가'에 가깝다.
notes: The taxonomy is explicitly a PILOT: the document states the list of goods, activities and sectors will be expanded later.

Unlike the EU and Korea, rows go down to the level of equipment, goods and services, and each row carries customs codes (ТН ВЭД and EU CN Code) alongside industry codes. This is because the taxonomy is tied to tax relief — VAT exemption under Art. 191 §7.2 of the Tax Code, plus income-tax exemption for holders of green bonds listed on the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange.

The industry column is labelled NACE 2.1, a different edition from the NACE Rev.2 used by the EU delegated acts; section letters differ between editions, so only the numeric division+group is carried over to ISIC.
One record per technology (Технология). The rows beneath it — function groups and components — are kept in the 'components' field.

Objective is recorded as climate_mitigation for all records: the table has no per-row objective column, and the document's stated purpose is decarbonisation. Adaptation is named as an aim of the taxonomy but not mapped row by row. TO VERIFY: whether any rows should be classed as adaptation.

profiles.name: UMOA Taxonomy of green, social and sustainable projects
profiles.issuer: Autorité des Marchés Financiers de l'UMOA (AMF-UMOA)
profiles.legal_basis: Circulaire N°001-AMF-UMOA/2024 relative à la taxonomie des projets verts, sociaux et durables au sein de l'UMOA, §8.2
profiles.structure_note_ko: 적격 프로젝트 '목록'이다. 대부분의 항목에 수치가 없으므로, 임계값형과는 '같은 활동을 인정하는가'까지만 비교할 수 있고 '더 엄격한가'는 비교 대상이 아니다.
notes: This is NOT a threshold taxonomy. The Circulaire lists eligible projects per sub-category and tags each row with SDG icons and a mitigation/adaptation label. Only six numeric conditions appear anywhere in the tables; they are recorded as thresholds with the French source wording kept verbatim.
Criteria are recorded as type 'eligible_projects', not 'substantial_contribution': the document states what may be financed, not the performance an activity must meet.

The source PDF is a scan with no text layer and no French OCR model was available, so the tables were transcribed by reading the page images. Threshold wording is verbatim; some project lines are condensed — see raw/UMOA_transcription.md.
The freight-transport figures are quoted by the Circulaire from the Climate Bonds Standard, not set by AMF-UMOA itself.
Social projects carry no climate objective in the source table; they are recorded with objective='social'.
Jurisdictions: UMOA has 8 member states. The Circulaire applies union-wide.

profiles.name: ASEAN Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
profiles.issuer: ASEAN Taxonomy Board (ATB)
profiles.structure_note_ko: 정성 판단 틀(FF)과 수치 기준 틀(PS)을 함께 둔다. 같은 활동이 어느 틀로 평가되느냐에 따라 결과가 달라지므로, 비교할 때 어느 틀인지 먼저 밝혀야 한다.
objectives_local: EO3 Protection of healthy ecosystems and biodiversity
EO4 Resource resilience and the transition to a circular economy
notes: Tiers 2 and 3 will be gradually sunset over time for all Activities; the stated aim is to migrate every Activity to Tier 1. This is a designed expiry, not a grandfathering clause.

Annex 1 Activities sit in ISIC 351 (electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply), 352 (transmission and distribution of renewable and low-carbon gases, including storage) and 353 (heating/cooling production, including thermal storage), plus two activities that are not in ISIC at all: 000[010] Transport of CO2 and 000[020] Underground permanent geological storage of CO2.
Coal phase-out (CPO) is itself a classifiable Activity under the ASEAN Taxonomy.

The document states the ASEAN Taxonomy was the main reference for Indonesia's ITSF (OJK, 2025) and the Philippine SFTG (BSP, 2024). This is the stated lineage of the Philippine framework recorded separately in phl.json.
Version history stated in the document: V2 published 27 March 2023, effective 19 February 2024; V4 dated 6 November 2025.

classification.label: Green
classification.rule: Result in a positive benefit to one or more Environmental Objectives, or create utility while displacing a provider of that utility which detracts from an EO. Green-FF under the Foundation Framework; Green-Tier 1 under the Plus Standard.

classification.label: Amber
classification.rule: Amber-FF under the Foundation Framework; Amber-Tier 2 and Amber-Tier 3 under the Plus Standard. An Activity is classified Amber if it is causing or may cause significant harm.

classification.label: Red
classification.rule: Not aligned with the ASEAN Taxonomy.

frames.name: Foundation Framework
frames.note: Qualitative, sector-agnostic screening criteria and a decision flow. No numeric thresholds. Yields Green-FF or Amber-FF.

frames.name: Plus Standard
frames.note: Technical Screening Criteria for 6 focus sectors and 3 enabling sectors, in Tiers 1-3. Yields Green-Tier 1, Amber-Tier 2, Amber-Tier 3.

focus_sectors: Electricity, Gas, Steam and Air Conditioning Supply
Water supply, Sewerage, Waste Management and Remediation

profiles.jurisdiction_note: The ASEAN Taxonomy applies across ASEAN Member States. It is recorded here for the two AMS that have no national taxonomy of their own (Brunei, Myanmar); the other AMS are carried under their national frameworks, which the ASEAN Taxonomy sits alongside.

profiles.name: Australian Sustainable Finance Taxonomy

profiles.name: Philippine Sustainable Finance Taxonomy Guidelines (SFTG)
profiles.issuer: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
profiles.legal_basis: BSP Circular No. 1187, Series of 2024 (Monetary Board Resolution No. 193, 14 February 2024), amending Sec. 153 of the Manual of Regulations for Banks
profiles.structure_note_ko: 활동 목록도 임계값도 없다. 분류 규칙과 유도질문으로 평가자가 판단한다. 비교 가능한 것은 분류 논리·목표 범위·피해 처리 방식이다.
future_objectives: Protection of healthy ecosystems and biodiversity
Promotion of resource resilience and transition to circular economy
notes: This is a principles-based taxonomy. There are no per-activity numeric thresholds to compare against the EU or Korea; what can be compared is the classification logic, the objectives covered, and the treatment of harm and transition.

The Amber class is the closest counterpart to Korea's 전환부문 (Transitional Area) and to the EU's transitional activities, but it works differently: the EU and Korea name transitional activities in advance with criteria attached, while the Philippines decides case by case on whether harm is remediable in time.

SOURCE TEXT QUALITY: the text available for this build came from OCR of a scanned circular and contains character errors. Nothing here is offered as a verbatim quotation. Any passage that needs to be quoted must be re-checked against the original PDF.
TO VERIFY: whether BSP has issued a born-digital version of the SFTG annex, which would allow verbatim extraction of Tables 7-12 (the guiding questions).

classification.label: Green
classification.rule: The activity makes a substantial contribution to an Environmental Objective and meets the Essential Criteria (DNSH and Minimum Social Safeguards).

classification.label: Amber
classification.rule: The activity makes a substantial contribution to an Environmental Objective but causes significant harm to another. It still qualifies if that harm can be remediated within 5 years, or an independent verification supports a claim that remediation will take less than 10 years, and the Essential Criteria of DNSH and MSS are met.

classification.label: Red
classification.rule: The activity does not serve any Environmental Objective or does not meet the Essential Criteria. A Red activity may still receive 'unlabelled' financing; the label does not imply the activity is unsustainable, only that it does not meet the SFTG's ambition.

essential_criteria.name: Do No Significant Harm
essential_criteria.note: An activity contributing substantially to one Environmental Objective must not significantly harm any other.

essential_criteria.name: Remedial Measures to Transition
essential_criteria.note: Measures that remove or render insignificant any actual or potential significant harm; specific time periods are allowed for an activity to become aligned. This is the mechanism behind the Amber class.

essential_criteria.name: Minimum Social Safeguards
essential_criteria.note: Compliance with national regulatory requirements, assessed at COMPANY level rather than activity level.

assessment.method: Guiding questions and a decision flow diagram, not numeric activity thresholds. The guidelines carry use cases for mitigation (Appendix 3) and adaptation (Appendix 4), a non-exhaustive list of Philippine laws for MSS (Appendix 1), and examples of industry standards and certifications (Appendix 5).
assessment.objective_choice: One Environmental Objective must be named as primary, even when both are listed.

profiles.applies_to: Banks — when extending credit, making investment decisions, and designing sustainable financial products and services
relationships: Certain definitions are borrowed and adapted from the ASEAN Taxonomy Version 2.
For sustainable bond issuance, banks follow the SEC's sustainable bond standards; the SFTG may be applied voluntarily on top of them.

msme_treatment.note: MSMEs are addressed separately. The Philippines defines MSMEs both by employment size (PSA) and by asset size (Magna Carta for MSMEs, as amended 2008); either may be applied under the SFTG.
msme_treatment.examples_source: IFC Sustainable MSME Finance Reference Guide
msme_treatment.examples_caveat: The guidelines state these are examples only and do not constitute automatic endorsement of alignment under the SFTG.

metrics_caveat: comparable=true only means more than one framework put a number on this activity. It does not mean the numbers measure the same thing — check each entry's metric, unit and verbatim text before saying one country is stricter.

metric_index.purpose: Every numeric threshold in the dataset, grouped by metric and value, so a question like 'which countries use 100 gCO2e/kWh?' can be answered directly.
caveats: Equal values do NOT mean equal criteria. The activity they attach to, the date they apply from, and the exceptions around them differ. Read each entry's verbatim text before saying two countries have the same rule.
A shared value very often means one framework copied the EU delegated acts. That lineage is worth stating, and it is also the reason the values match.

Percentage thresholds are NOT grouped by value: a percentage means something different in every criterion (emission savings, efficiency, recycled content, leakage reduction). They are listed per framework instead, under 'percent_by_framework'.
'kind' says whether the sentence reads as a taxonomy criterion or as national-policy context (an NDC target, for example). Only quote 'criterion' entries as thresholds.

Construcción y operación de la conexión directa, o expansión de la conexión directa existente, de generación de electricidad con bajas emisiones de carbono por debajo del umbral de 100 gCO2e / kWh medido sobre la base del ciclo de vida a una subestación o red. b.

crosswalk.method: ISIC group must match, then Jaccard similarity of normalised activity-name terms (Cyrillic transliterated, French and Russian function words dropped, synonyms folded to English); score >= 0.5 confident, 0.25-0.5 needs human review, below that weak. 'curated' links were checked by reading both names.
crosswalk.caveat: A link means the two frameworks describe the same kind of activity. It does NOT mean the criteria are equivalent — comparing the criteria is the point of the link. In particular a link between a threshold framework (EU, Korea) and an activity-list framework (UMOA, Kyrgyzstan) connects an activity to a project category, and only one side has numbers.

framework.jurisdiction_note: The ASEAN Taxonomy applies across ASEAN Member States. It is recorded here for the two AMS that have no national taxonomy of their own (Brunei, Myanmar); the other AMS are carried under their national frameworks, which the ASEAN Taxonomy sits alongside.

classification.label: Green
classification.rule: Result in a positive benefit to one or more Environmental Objectives, or create utility while displacing a provider of that utility which detracts from an EO. Green-FF under the Foundation Framework; Green-Tier 1 under the Plus Standard.

classification.label: Amber
classification.rule: Amber-FF under the Foundation Framework; Amber-Tier 2 and Amber-Tier 3 under the Plus Standard. An Activity is classified Amber if it is causing or may cause significant harm.

classification.label: Red
classification.rule: Not aligned with the ASEAN Taxonomy.

frames.name: Foundation Framework
frames.note: Qualitative, sector-agnostic screening criteria and a decision flow. No numeric thresholds. Yields Green-FF or Amber-FF.

frames.name: Plus Standard
frames.note: Technical Screening Criteria for 6 focus sectors and 3 enabling sectors, in Tiers 1-3. Yields Green-Tier 1, Amber-Tier 2, Amber-Tier 3.

framework.name: Australian Sustainable Finance Taxonomy
framework.issuer: Australian Sustainable Finance Institute (ASFI); governance oversight by the Council of Financial Regulators' Climate Working Group (Treasury, RBA, APRA, ASIC)

dnsh_objectives.local: A. Climate change adaptation and resilience
C. Sustainable use and protection of water resources
E. Transition to a circular economy

assessment.method: Initial development phase covers climate change mitigation criteria for six priority sectors, plus a DNSH framework and Minimum Social Safeguards.
assessment.dnsh_structure: DNSH applies at ACTIVITY level and considers potential and actual impacts across the whole lifecycle of an asset, activity or project. It has two layers: generic criteria (principles-based, one set per environmental objective) and specific criteria (particular requirements).
assessment.mandatory: Voluntary. ASFI makes the initial taxonomy available for use by firms, investors and regulators on a voluntary basis; government review of it and of possible use cases was scheduled separately.

notes: Only climate change mitigation has substantial-contribution criteria; the other five objectives appear only as DNSH objectives. This is the same shape as Singapore and Fiji.

Sectors with technical screening criteria in the document include electricity generation and supply, minerals/mining and metals, manufacturing and industry, agriculture and land, construction and buildings, and transport.
Australia's mandatory climate DISCLOSURE regime (from 1 January 2025) is separate from the taxonomy, which is voluntary. Do not conflate the two.

59 Criterios de contribución sustancial Las emisiones de GEI del ciclo de vida de la generación de energía a partir de la fuente geotérmica deben ser inferiores a 100 gCO2e/ kWh.
Por eso, es importante demostrar que las emisiones de GEI son inferiores a 100gCO2e/kWh en su ciclo de vida para que estén alineados.

El metano extraído se emplea para producir energía térmica, mecánica o simplemente eléctrica Criterios de contribución sustancial Todas las instalaciones deben demostrar que operan con emisiones de ciclo de vida inferiores al umbral vigente (100 gCO2e/kWh), por medio del cumplimiento de la ISO 14067 o de un producto del protocolo de GEI, como el Product Carbon Footprint (PCF).

Al establecer un umbral de emisiones inferior a 100gCO2e/kWh y requerir que la biomasa provenga de fuentes sostenibles, se garantiza que la generación de bioenergía contribuya efectivamente a la mitigación del cambio climático sin comprometer los ecosistemas ni la seguridad alimentaria.

El factor de emisiones de la red del sistema promedio, calculado como las emisiones anuales totales de la generación de energía conectada al sistema, dividido por la producción de electricidad neta anual total en ese sistema, está por debajo del valor umbral de 100 gCO2e/ kWh en su ciclo de vida de acuerdo con los criterios de generación de electricidad, durante un período de cinco años móviles.

Construcción y operación de la conexión directa, o expansión de la conexión directa existente, de generación de electricidad con bajas emisiones de carbono por debajo del umbral de 100 gCO2e / kWh medido sobre la base del ciclo de vida a una subestación o red. b.

framework.name: Fiji Green Finance Taxonomy

notes: Initial focus is climate change mitigation only; the document states future iterations are expected to add climate change adaptation and resilience and the protection and restoration of Fiji's marine ecosystems — the marine objective being the distinctive one for Fiji.

Hydropower criteria mirror the EU's: run-of-river with no artificial reservoir, power density above 5 W/m2, or GHG intensity under 100 gCO2e/kWh.
Annex 1 gives decarbonisation pathways for different ship types — the same annex structure as Cambodia's taxonomy, which shares the IFC-supported drafting lineage.

framework.name: Ghana Green Finance Taxonomy (Phase One)

assessment.method: Technical screening criteria built on five pillars: climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, environmental protection, resource efficiency and pollution prevention. DNSH and minimum social safeguards apply.

notes: PHASE ONE IS QUALITATIVE. The document states the rollout is phased: Phase 1 develops qualitative criteria for the selected sectors; Phase 2 introduces QUANTITATIVE THRESHOLDS, tax exemptions and sector-based incentives (stated target: May 2025); Phase 3 develops a transitional taxonomy covering carbon-intensive sectors such as oil, gas and mining. So a question about Ghana's numeric thresholds has no answer in this version — say so.

framework.name: Green Taxonomy of the Kyrgyz Republic (pilot national classifier)
framework.issuer: Kyrgyz Republic (Приложение — пилотный общенациональный классификатор)
notes: The taxonomy is explicitly a PILOT: the document states the list of goods, activities and sectors will be expanded later.

Unlike the EU and Korea, rows go down to the level of equipment, goods and services, and each row carries customs codes (ТН ВЭД and EU CN Code) alongside industry codes. This is because the taxonomy is tied to tax relief — VAT exemption under Art. 191 §7.2 of the Tax Code, plus income-tax exemption for holders of green bonds listed on the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange.

The industry column is labelled NACE 2.1, a different edition from the NACE Rev.2 used by the EU delegated acts; section letters differ between editions, so only the numeric division+group is carried over to ISIC.
One record per technology (Технология). The rows beneath it — function groups and components — are kept in the 'components' field.

Objective is recorded as climate_mitigation for all records: the table has no per-row objective column, and the document's stated purpose is decarbonisation. Adaptation is named as an aim of the taxonomy but not mapped row by row. TO VERIFY: whether any rows should be classed as adaptation.

framework.name: Sustainable Finance Taxonomy for the Cambodian Banking Sector
framework.issuer: National Bank of Cambodia (NBC)

classification.label: Green (aligned)
classification.rule: Substantial contribution to the specified environmental objective — either already at or near zero emissions, or on a clearly defined Paris-aligned decarbonisation pathway.

classification.label: Amber (transitional)
classification.rule: Not yet at or near net zero, but contributing to substantial emission reductions on a credible decarbonisation pathway towards the Green criteria. Subject to specific performance thresholds and SUNSET DATES, by which they must meet Green criteria to remain aligned. Equivalent to Tier 2 and Tier 3 of the ASEAN Plus Standard.

classification.label: Red
classification.rule: Not aligned.

assessment.method: Sectoral Decarbonization Approach (SDA), using IEA, IPCC and IIASA scenarios. The Green threshold follows the 1.5°C pathway; the Amber threshold follows the non-OECD NDC-based pathway (Transition Pathway Initiative, 2021).

notes: Dated April 2026 — newer than most national taxonomies in this dataset.

The document notes that technical screening criteria are often NOT defined for most waste management activities, and that numeric criteria are used where eligibility needs them (hydropower is the example given) and to draw the Amber/Red boundary.
Includes Annex 2 on the early and managed phase-out of coal-fired power plants, and Annex 3 a whitelist of activities.

framework.name: Philippine Sustainable Finance Taxonomy Guidelines (SFTG)
framework.issuer: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
framework.legal_basis: BSP Circular No. 1187, Series of 2024 (Monetary Board Resolution No. 193, 14 February 2024), amending Sec. 153 of the Manual of Regulations for Banks
framework.developed_by: Financial Sector Forum (FSF), following the Philippine Sustainable Finance Roadmap issued by the inter-agency Green Force in October 2021
framework.applies_to: Banks — when extending credit, making investment decisions, and designing sustainable financial products and services
future_objectives: Protection of healthy ecosystems and biodiversity
Promotion of resource resilience and transition to circular economy

classification.label: Green
classification.rule: The activity makes a substantial contribution to an Environmental Objective and meets the Essential Criteria (DNSH and Minimum Social Safeguards).

classification.label: Amber
classification.rule: The activity makes a substantial contribution to an Environmental Objective but causes significant harm to another. It still qualifies if that harm can be remediated within 5 years, or an independent verification supports a claim that remediation will take less than 10 years, and the Essential Criteria of DNSH and MSS are met.

classification.label: Red
classification.rule: The activity does not serve any Environmental Objective or does not meet the Essential Criteria. A Red activity may still receive 'unlabelled' financing; the label does not imply the activity is unsustainable, only that it does not meet the SFTG's ambition.

essential_criteria.name: Do No Significant Harm
essential_criteria.note: An activity contributing substantially to one Environmental Objective must not significantly harm any other.

essential_criteria.name: Remedial Measures to Transition
essential_criteria.note: Measures that remove or render insignificant any actual or potential significant harm; specific time periods are allowed for an activity to become aligned. This is the mechanism behind the Amber class.

essential_criteria.name: Minimum Social Safeguards
essential_criteria.note: Compliance with national regulatory requirements, assessed at COMPANY level rather than activity level.

assessment.method: Guiding questions and a decision flow diagram, not numeric activity thresholds. The guidelines carry use cases for mitigation (Appendix 3) and adaptation (Appendix 4), a non-exhaustive list of Philippine laws for MSS (Appendix 1), and examples of industry standards and certifications (Appendix 5).
assessment.objective_choice: One Environmental Objective must be named as primary, even when both are listed.

msme_treatment.note: MSMEs are addressed separately. The Philippines defines MSMEs both by employment size (PSA) and by asset size (Magna Carta for MSMEs, as amended 2008); either may be applied under the SFTG.
msme_treatment.examples_source: IFC Sustainable MSME Finance Reference Guide
msme_treatment.examples_caveat: The guidelines state these are examples only and do not constitute automatic endorsement of alignment under the SFTG.

relationships: Certain definitions are borrowed and adapted from the ASEAN Taxonomy Version 2.
For sustainable bond issuance, banks follow the SEC's sustainable bond standards; the SFTG may be applied voluntarily on top of them.
notes: This is a principles-based taxonomy. There are no per-activity numeric thresholds to compare against the EU or Korea; what can be compared is the classification logic, the objectives covered, and the treatment of harm and transition.

The Amber class is the closest counterpart to Korea's 전환부문 (Transitional Area) and to the EU's transitional activities, but it works differently: the EU and Korea name transitional activities in advance with criteria attached, while the Philippines decides case by case on whether harm is remediable in time.

SOURCE TEXT QUALITY: the text available for this build came from OCR of a scanned circular and contains character errors. Nothing here is offered as a verbatim quotation. Any passage that needs to be quoted must be re-checked against the original PDF.
TO VERIFY: whether BSP has issued a born-digital version of the SFTG annex, which would allow verbatim extraction of Tables 7-12 (the guiding questions).

framework.name: Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
framework.issuer: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS); developed by the Green Finance Industry Taskforce (GFIT), succeeded by the Singapore Sustainable Finance Association

objectives.local: Promote resource resilience and circular economy

classification.label: Green
classification.rule: Environmentally sustainable.

classification.label: Amber
classification.rule: Transition. Amber thresholds carry SUNSET DATES.

classification.label: Ineligible
classification.rule: Neither Green nor Amber. Note the third class is called 'Ineligible', not 'Red'.

assessment.method: Activities are defined on ISIC level 3. Criteria are set per activity as a traffic-light table (Green / Amber / Ineligible) with an interoperability reference, most often the EU Taxonomy.
assessment.dnsh_status: DNSH is currently BEST-PRACTICE DISCLOSURE in the early implementation phase, not an eligibility condition. The document says it could be incorporated into eligibility in future.
assessment.mandatory: Not mandatory and not contained in any regulation at the time of publishing; intended to be voluntary in its first years.

notes: Only climate change mitigation has economic activities and technical screening criteria so far. The other four objectives are stated as future iterations — so a question about, say, Singapore's water criteria has no answer in this document yet.

The criteria blocks are therefore stored unassigned, with their own text, and pairing needs a human pass or a layout-aware re-extraction.
Explicitly designed to be interoperable with the EU Taxonomy and the ASEAN Taxonomy; many criteria cite 'EU Taxonomy' as their reference.

thresholds.verbatim: The country submitted its first Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in 2016, committing to a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the projected business-as-usual (BAU) level by 2030, with the potential to increase this to 25% conditional on international support.

At COP26 in Glasgow, the Prime Minister announced an enhanced target of carbon neutrality by 2050 and reaffirmed the net-zero goal by 2065, with the potential to raise emission reductions to 40% by 2030, contingent on adequate international support 6 .
In November 2022, Thailand Second Updated NDC 7 and the revised LT-LEDs 8 , committing to a 30% GHG reduction by 2030, with an enhanced ambition of up to 40% under favorable conditions.
According to the draft National Energy Plan, at least 50% of new power generation will be renewable by 2050, with solar and wind projected to contribute 65% of total electricity generation by 2060.
With full support, this would represent a 60% reduction from 2019 levels, potentially aligning Thailand with a pathway to limit global temperature rise to 1.5°C.

notes: This is NOT a threshold taxonomy. The Circulaire lists eligible projects per sub-category and tags each row with SDG icons and a mitigation/adaptation label. Only six numeric conditions appear anywhere in the tables; they are recorded as thresholds with the French source wording kept verbatim.
Criteria are recorded as type 'eligible_projects', not 'substantial_contribution': the document states what may be financed, not the performance an activity must meet.

The source PDF is a scan with no text layer and no French OCR model was available, so the tables were transcribed by reading the page images. Threshold wording is verbatim; some project lines are condensed — see raw/UMOA_transcription.md.
The freight-transport figures are quoted by the Circulaire from the Climate Bonds Standard, not set by AMF-UMOA itself.
Social projects carry no climate objective in the source table; they are recorded with objective='social'.
Jurisdictions: UMOA has 8 member states. The Circulaire applies union-wide.

framework.name: South African Green Finance Taxonomy
framework.issuer: National Treasury — Taxonomy Working Group, under South Africa's Sustainable Finance Initiative

objectives.local: Sustainable use of water and marine resources

assessment.method: A seven-step alignment process: … Step 4 meet the applicable Technical Screening Criteria; Step 5 Principle 2 — do no significant harm to any other objective; Step 6 Principle 3 — comply with Minimum Social Safeguards; Step 7 conclude on taxonomic alignment.
assessment.generic_dnsh: Appendices A and D-F give generic DNSH criteria per objective, and Appendix C the Minimum Social Safeguards.

notes: Structurally the closest of this group to the EU Taxonomy: substantial contribution + DNSH + minimum social safeguards, with generic DNSH criteria per objective in appendices.

Many thresholds are visibly lifted from the EU delegated acts (for example the '10% most efficient installations in 2016 and 2017' benchmark). Where a value carries a comma, read it as the EU does — a decimal point.
The document uses South Africa's own SIC codes rather than ISIC.
